The root user has unrestricted access to TODOS account features and settings AWS — including actions other than policies IAM can block (such as closing the account, changing billing settings, cancel support) — and cannot have your permissions limited by police IAM

saa-ini-206.text: A company has an application running in EC2 who needs to communicate with the DynamoDB. The instance is in a private sub-network (no internet access). The team realized that calls to DynamoDB What's stopping communication??
options: The DynamoDB is a public service with endpoint on the internet — instances in private sub-networks without NAT Gateway or VPC Endpoint cannot reach the public endpoint of DynamoDB, resulting in timeout in calls from API
The Security Group of the instance EC2 needs an output rule for IP of DynamoDB at the door 443 — without that rule, traffic HTTPS is blocked by SG
The DynamoDB requires calls to be made from instances in the same AZ — an instance in an AZ different from the table DynamoDB Can't communicate
A IAM Role of the court is not allowed to access the DynamoDB — the connection error is caused by lack of authorization, not by network connectivity
saa-ini-206.explanation: Correct. DynamoDB is a regional service accessed via endpoints HTTPS public. Fora in private sub-networks without route to the internet (without NAT Gateway/Internet Gateway) The solution is to create a VPC Endpoint DynamoDB (Gateway Endpoint, free of charge) or use a NAT Gateway.
saa-ini-206.hint: The DynamoDB is accessed via endpoint HTTPS public. Fora in private sub-networks need what mechanism to achieve services AWS public without internet?
optionRationales: Correct. DynamoDB is a regional service accessed via endpoints HTTPS public. Fora in private sub-networks without route to the internet (without NAT Gateway/Internet Gateway) The solution is to create a VPC Endpoint DynamoDB (Gateway Endpoint, free of charge) or use a NAT Gateway.

Incorrect. Security Groups EC2 by default allow all output traffic — the standard output rule is 'Allow All Outbound'. The problem is not the Security Group, but the lack of network route for the DynamoDB (no NAT Gateway nor VPC Endpoint). Even with SG released, no route is connectivity.

Incorrect. DynamoDB it has no restriction of AZ for access — it is a regional service accessible from any AZ of the region via the regional endpoint of the service. The barrier is not AZ, but the network connectivity (no route to the public endpoint).

Incorrect as primary cause. Lack of permission IAM would result in a mistake 403 (AccessDenied) — no connection timeout. saa-ini-207.text: A company is setting up its environment AWS for the first time. The architect wants to separate the resources of development, staging and production to prevent changes in development affect the production. AWS for this separation of environments?
options: Create accounts AWS separate for each environment (dev, staging, production) — separate accounts provide complete security, billing and resource insulation, preventing errors in one account from impacting the other
Use tags on all resources to identify the environment (e.g. 'Environment: Production') and configure policies IAM that check these tags before allowing actions — tags logically separate environments
Use S3 Subject Lock e SCP to block accidental modification production resources — the lock ensures that dev and production do not interfere with each other
Create separate VPCs within the same account AWS for each environment — different VPCs provide complete network insulation, preventing any communication between environments
saa-ini-207.explanation: Correct. AWS recommends using separate accounts for environment isolation. AWS are the strongest isolation unit: safety (policies) IAM do not cross accounts by default), separate billing (cost per environment visibility), and limited radius blast (an incident in dev cannot affect prod). They can be centrally managed via AWS Organizations.
saa-ini-207.hint: What is the strongest isolation unit in the AWS — that separates resources completely, IAM, billing and blast radius between environments?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS recommends using separate accounts for environment isolation. AWS are the strongest isolation unit: safety (policies) IAM do not cross accounts by default), separate billing (cost per environment visibility), and limited radius blast (an incident in dev cannot affect prod). They can be centrally managed via AWS Organizations.

Partly useful for organization, but insufficient for real isolation. Tags are metadata — a user with account access can still interact with resources from any environment marked with different tags. Account separation guarantees technical isolation that tags do not provide (a deployment error in dev cannot affect prod if they are in different accounts).

Incorrect as complete isolation. Different VPCs in the same account still share the same namespace IAM, service limit, combined billing, and a user IAM with wide permissions can access resources in any VPC separate accounts provide stronger security insulation.

Incorrect. S3 Object Lock is for object immutability S3 (WORM), non-separation of environments. SCPs require AWS Organizations and control account permissions/OR — do not separate environments within an account. Separate accounts are the correct isolation mechanism.

saa-ini-208.text: A user forgot his account password IAM and can't access the console AWS. Who can redefine the user's password IAM?
options: Passwords IAM cannot be redefined without access — the user needs to be excluded and a new user created with the same policy
The user needs to use the 'I forgot my password' link on the login page of AWS, which will send a redefining email to the registered address in IAM
Only the technical support of the AWS can redefine passwords IAM — it is necessary to open a support ticket for access recovery
A user IAM administrator (with permission) iam:UpdateLoginProfile) or the account root user can reset the password of any user IAM
saa-ini-208.explanation: Correct. User passwords IAM can be redefined by any user with permission iam:UpdateLoginProfile — usually an administrator IAM or the account root itself. The root user has unrestricted access and can always reset user passwords IAM.
saa-ini-208.hint: Who in an account AWS is allowed to use iam:UpdateLoginProfile to redefine passwords for other users IAM?
optionRationales: Correct. User passwords IAM can be redefined by any user with permission iam:UpdateLoginProfile — usually an administrator IAM or the account root itself. The root user has unrestricted access and can always reset user passwords IAM.

Incorrect. AWS does not have access to customer accounts to redefine passwords IAM — this would be a violation of the shared responsibility model. IAM is the responsibility of the customer and can be done by an administrator of his own account.

Incorrect. The option of 'I forgot my password' on the login page of AWS Console is for the user ROOT account (using e-mail + password), not for users IAM. Users IAM have a URL account-specific login and do not have automatic password recovery by email — need an administrator to redefine.

Incorrect. User passwords IAM can be redefined without excluding the user — via iam:UpdateLoginProfile. Delete and recreate the user would cause loss of assigned policies and audit history, being unnecessary and not recommended.

saa-ini-209.text: A company wants to ensure that data stored in buckets S3 are always encrypted. What is the simplest way to ensure that TODOS the new objects in a pocket are encrypted automatically, without the customer specifying encryption in each upload?
options: Configure S3 Versioning — the versioning of the S3 automatically encrypts all versions of stored objects
Create a Bucket Policy with Deny in s3:PutObject for any upload — it forces developers to use the console AWS which always encrypts automatically

Configure Standard Encryption (Default Encryption) in the pocket S3 — o S3 will automatically apply SSE-S3 (or SSE-KMS if configured) to all objects sent without encryption specification, ensuring that no object is left without encryption
Enable Amazon Macie in the pocket — or Macie detects unencrypted data and automatically encrypts existing and new objects
saa-ini-209.explanation: Correct. S3 (Default Encryption) ensures that objects without explicit cryptography instruction on upload are automatically encrypted by S3. This protects against accidental uploads without encryption. S3 use SSE-S3 (managed by S3) which has no additional cost.
saa-ini-209.hint: What configuration of the S3 makes the service itself apply encryption automatically to all objects sent without encryption specification?
optionRationales: Correct. S3 (Default Encryption) ensures that objects without explicit cryptography instruction on upload are automatically encrypted by S3. This protects against accidental uploads without encryption. S3 use SSE-S3 (managed by S3) which has no additional cost.
Incorrect. Denying all PutObject would block any upload (encrypted or not), making the bucket unusable. AWS not 'always automatically encrypt' by default without Default Encryption configuration.

Incorrect. Amazon Macie is a sensitive data discovery service (detecta) PII, (c) — is not a cryptographic service. Macie does not encrypt objects. S3 is the correct mechanism for automatic encryption.

Incorrect. S3 Versioning maintains multiple versions of an object over time — it has no connection with encryption. Versioning and encryption are independent resources in S3. Default Encryption is the right mechanism to ensure automatic encryption.

saa-ini-210.text: A company uses AWS IAM and wants to understand the difference between a IAM Identity-based policy and resource-based policy. What statement correctly describes this difference?
options: Identity-based policies apply only to the web console of AWS; resource-based policies apply only to access via CLI and SDK — the division is through the access channel
Identity-based policies have priority over resource-based policies when there is conflict — identity policy always prevails

Identity-based policies are attached to users, groups or roles IAM and control what this identity PODE FAZER; resource-based policies are attached directly to resources (e.g.: S3) and control QUEM PODE ACESSAR this resource — the main difference is the annexation point
Resource-based policies exist only in S3 — other services AWS exclusively use identity-based policies for access control
saa-ini-210.explanation: Identity-based policies are defined from the perspective of IDENTIDADE (what this user/role can do). Resource-based policies are defined from the perspective of RECURSO (For example: a bucket policy in the S3 is a resource-based policy that lists the mains that can access the pocket — very common for cross-account access.
saa-ini-210.hint: Where (in what) each type of policy is attached — and what perspective each represents (identity or recourse))?
optionRationales: Identity-based policies are defined from the perspective of IDENTIDADE (what this user/role can do). Resource-based policies are defined from the perspective of RECURSO (For example: a bucket policy in the S3 is a resource-based policy that lists the mains that can access the pocket — very common for cross-account access.

Incorrect. The type of policy (identity-based vs resource-based) has no relation to the access channel (console vs. CLI vs SDK). Both types are evaluated on any call from API, regardless of how the call is made.

There's no simple hierarchy where a guy always prevails. IAM, an explicit Deny in QUALQUER For access within the same account, the IAM evaluation TODAS the applicable policies (identity and resource) and grants access only if at least one allows and no denies. For cross-account access, AMBAS need to allow.

Incorrect. Many services AWS support resource-based policies beyond the S3: SNS (topic policies), SQS (I'm sorry, I'm sorry.), Lambda (Police function), KMS (key policies), Secrets Manager, API Gateway, among others. The list of services that support resource-based policies is extensive.

saa-ini-211.text: A startup is creating its first environment AWS. The architect recommended creating a VPC customized instead of using the VPC standard. What is the VPC Standard (Default VPC) which exists in each region AWS?
options: A VPC Standard is one VPC shared between all accounts AWS in the same region — all accounts access the same VPC Standard and its resources
There's no VPC Standard — each account starts without any VPC and the administrator needs to create the first VPC before any appeal is brought
A VPC Pattern has CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 and needs to be manually configured by the administrator with subnets and routes before it can be used

A VPC Standard is automatically created by AWS in each region when the account is created — has CIDR 172.31.0.0/16, a public sub-network by AZ, a Internet Gateway attached, and route tables configured for internet access; instances released in it have public IPs by default
saa-ini-211.explanation: Correct. VPC has the characteristics: CIDR 172.31.0.0/16, a sub-network /20 by AZ (all public by default), a Internet Gateway attached, and route tables that direct 0.0.0.0/0 for the IGW. Fora launched in default subnets VPC receive public IP automatically. It is designed to facilitate fast start, but is not recommended for production.
saa-ini-211.hint: A VPC Pattern comes pre-configured with which CIDR range and already has what kind of connected gateway that allows internet access?
optionRationales: Correct. VPC has the characteristics: CIDR 172.31.0.0/16, a sub-network /20 by AZ (all public by default), a Internet Gateway attached, and route tables that direct 0.0.0.0/0 for the IGW. Fora launched in default subnets VPC receive public IP automatically. It is designed to facilitate fast start, but is not recommended for production.

Incorrect. VPC has CIDR 172.31.0.0/16 (no 10.0.0.0/16) and already fully configured with public subnets, Internet Gateway and routes — does not require manual configuration for basic use. 10.0.0.0/16 is the CIDR commonly used in customised VPCs (but not fixed)).

Incorrect. AWS has one VPC Standard created automatically in each region. VPC exists to facilitate fast start — new users can launch instances EC2 immediately without need to create network infrastructure first.

Incorrect. AWS Has your own. VPC Standard — they are isolated from each other. There is no sharing of VPC between different accounts by default (this would require explicit configuration via Resource Access Manager or VPC Peering/Transit Gateway).

saa-ini-212.text: A company uses instances EC2 in one VPC with Security Groups set up. An administrator wants to understand how standard output rules (outbound) work Security Group What is the standard output behavior of a Security Group new?
options: A new one Security Group allows TODO the standard output traffic (rule 'Allow All Outbound' for 0.0.0.0/0 all doors) — and blocks all entry traffic by default (without entry rules)
A new one Security Group allows all traffic both input and output by default — it is the administrator that needs to add restriction rules
A new one Security Group block all traffic both input and output by default — the administrator needs to explicitly create all necessary rules
The standard rules of Security Group depend on the type of instance — web instances have door 80/443 open by default, database instances have door 3306, And so on
saa-ini-212.explanation: By default, one Security Group Newborn has: (1) No entry rules — all entry traffic is blocked; (2) An output rule that allows all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 — all outbound traffic is allowed. This reflects the principle that instances can communicate with the external world by default, but the external world cannot initiate connections with instances..
saa-ini-212.hint: For one Security Group newly created, which direction of traffic (entry or exit) is allowed by default, and which is blocked by default?
optionRationales: By default, one Security Group Newborn has: (1) No entry rules — all entry traffic is blocked; (2) An output rule that allows all traffic to 0.0.0.0/0 — all outbound traffic is allowed. This reflects the principle that instances can communicate with the external world by default, but the external world cannot initiate connections with instances..

Incorrect. Although the input is blocked by default, the SAID is not — there is a standard rule that allows all output traffic. This makes it easy for instances to start connections with other features (e.g., patch download) without additional configuration.

Incorrect. ENTRADA is blocked by default in new Security Groups — no entry rules exist. Only output is allowed by default. If entry was allowed by default, any port would be exposed before the administrator set rules.

Incorrect. The standard rules of Security Group They don't depend on the kind of instance. Security Group new has the same pattern: locked entry (without rules), permitted exit (rule Allow All). The type of instance does not influence the rules of Security Group.

saa-ini-213.text: A company wants to implement authentication of two factors for users who access the console AWS. What service/functionality of the AWS allows this for users IAM?
options: The console AWS already requires MFA by default for all accounts — no additional configuration required
AWS Cognito — creates pools of users with MFA enabled for the console AWS

IAM Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) — combines a device MFA virtual (authenticator app) or physical (hardware token) to a user IAM; after enabled, the user needs to provide code of MFA plus password to access the console
AWS Single Sign-On (IAM Identity Center) — is the only service that supports MFA for the console AWS, being mandatory to enable authentication of two factors
saa-ini-213.explanation: Correct. IAM supports MFA for users IAM natively. The administrator can enable MFA per user or create policies that require MFA for certain actions. Virtual devices (Google Authenticator, Authy), tokens TOTP Of hardware, and keys FIDO2 are supported.
saa-ini-213.hint: What native functionality of IAM adds a second layer of verification (in addition to password) for access to the console AWS?
optionRationales: Correct. IAM supports MFA for users IAM natively. The administrator can enable MFA per user or create policies that require MFA for certain actions. Virtual devices (Google Authenticator, Authy), tokens TOTP Of hardware, and keys FIDO2 are supported.

Incorrect. Amazon Cognito is for authentication of users in web/mobile applications (not the console AWS). The console AWS use IAM for authentication of account users. Cognito does not manage users IAM no access to the console AWS.

Incorrect. IAM supports MFA native to users IAM — does not require IAM Identity Center. The Identity Center is for corporate identity federation and SSO (Unified access to multiple accounts/applications), but MFA for users IAM simple can be enabled directly in IAM.

saa-ini-214.text: A developer wants to access resources AWS via command line (AWS CLI). What kind of credentials do you have? IAM the developer needs to set up on your computer to authenticate calls from API way CLI?
options: The console password IAM user — same password used to access the web console AWS is used to authenticate the CLI
Access Key ID and Secret Access Key — a pair of access keys created in IAM for the user; or AWS CLI uses these keys to sign cryptographically calls from API and authenticate the user next to the AWS
The ARN (Amazon User Resource Name) IAM — o CLI use the ARN as unique identifier to authenticate calls
A token IAM generated at each session via the console AWS — the token is copied to the computer and configured in CLI for the current session
saa-ini-214.explanation: Correct. AWS CLI Use Access Keys (Access Key ID + Secret Access Key) for program authentication. Keys are configured with 'aws configures and is stored in the file ~/.aws/credentials. Each pair of keys is unique per user IAM and can be created/disabled on the console IAM.
saa-ini-214.hint: What kind of credentials do you have? IAM is designed for programmatic access (CLI, SDK, APIs) — different from the password used for the web console?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS CLI Use Access Keys (Access Key ID + Secret Access Key) for program authentication. Keys are configured with 'aws configures and is stored in the file ~/.aws/credentials. Each pair of keys is unique per user IAM and can be created/disabled on the console IAM.

Incorrect. The console password IAM is used APENAS for login in the web console of AWS. For programmatic access via CLI, SDK or APIs, Access Keys (Access Key ID + Secret Access Key) — are different credentials for different purposes.

Incorrect. This process of 'copying session token' may confuse with temporary credentials of STS (used with roles), but it is not the default process to configure the CLI. The default configuration of the CLI Uses Access Keys Permanent. Temporary credentials are generated by programs like 'aws not manually copied.

Incorrect. ARN identify a resource IAM (like arn:aws:iam::123456789:user/joao), but it is not a authentication credentials. ARN has no associated cryptographic secret — cannot be used to authenticate calls from API. Access Keys are the correct credentials.

saa-ini-215.text: A company wants its web application to use HTTPS with a certificate SSL/TLS managed by AWS, without having to manage renewals manually. AWS provides certificates SSL/TLS managed with automatic renewal?
options: Amazon CloudFront — certified provisioning and management SSL/TLS automatically for all distributions created

AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) — issues, manages and automatically renews certificates SSL/TLS for use with services AWS (ALB, CloudFront, API Gateway); with validation DNS, the renewal is completely automatic without manual intervention
Amazon Route 53 — as a service DNS of AWS, o Route 53 issue and renew certificates automatically SSL/TLS for domains registered in it
AWS IAM — allows import and storage of certificates SSL/TLS which are automatically managed and renewed by IAM
saa-ini-215.explanation: Correct. AWS ACM issue certificates SSL/TLS free (for use with resources) AWS supported) and automatically renews them before maturity when validation DNS is configured. The certificate is associated with ALB, CloudFront or API Gateway — No Need to Manage Renewals.
saa-ini-215.hint: What service AWS was created specifically to provide, manage and automatically renew certificates SSL/TLS for use with services AWS?
optionRationales: Correct. AWS ACM issue certificates SSL/TLS free (for use with resources) AWS supported) and automatically renews them before maturity when validation DNS is configured. The certificate is associated with ALB, CloudFront or API Gateway — No Need to Manage Renewals.

Incorrect. Route 53 is a service of DNS and domain registration — does not issue certificates SSL/TLS. The ACM is the service for certificate management. Route 53 is often used in conjunction with the ACM for validation DNS of the certificate, but they are different services.

Incorrect. IAM may store imported certificates (from external CAs) for use with some legacy services, but does not issue certificates or renew them automatically. ACM is the modern service for certificate management with automatic renewal.

Incorrect. CloudFront can use certificates ACM (managed by ACM) or the standard certificate CloudFront, but the CloudFront by itself is not a certificate management service. ACM issuing and renewing — the CloudFront only use the certificate provided by ACM.

saa-ini-216.text: A company uses Amazon VPC and wants to understand the difference between Public Sub-network and Private Sub-network. What is the characteristic that defines whether a sub-network is public or private?
options: A sub-network is public when its CIDR range starts with 10.0.0.x (low addresses) and private when starting with 10.0.1.x (high addresses) — is an IP numbering convention
A subnet is public when your route table has a route to a Internet Gateway (0.0.0.0/0 → igw-xxx) — without this route, the subnet is private and instances in it cannot directly access the internet
A sub-network is public when the S3 Block Public Access is disabled for resources in it — Block Public Access determines the 'advertisement' of a sub-network
A subnet is public when it has a Security Group with the door 80 and 443 open for 0.0.0.0/0 — the rules of Security Group define whether the sub-network is public
saa-ini-216.explanation: Correct. The sub-network classification as public or private is determined by TABELA OF ROTAS — specifically if there is a standard route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to a Internet Gateway (IGW). Without this route, instances in the sub-network have no way to the Internet, making it 'private'. The name 'public' or 'private' is a convention — technically it is the presence/absence of the route to the IGW determining accessibility.
saa-ini-216.hint: What determines whether a sub-network is public or private — the CIDR, the SG rules, or the route table?
optionRationales: Correct. The sub-network classification as public or private is determined by TABELA OF ROTAS — specifically if there is a standard route (0.0.0.0/0) pointing to a Internet Gateway (IGW). Without this route, instances in the sub-network have no way to the Internet, making it 'private'. The name 'public' or 'private' is a convention — technically it is the presence/absence of the route to the IGW determining accessibility.
Incorrect. CIDR which defines public vs. private — it is the route table that determines this. 10.0.0.x e 10.0.1.x can be both public and private depending on the route tables associated with them.

Incorrect. S3 Block Public Access is a bucket configuration S3 for object access control — has no relation to sub-network classification VPC as public or private. The sub-network classification is purely based on the route tables..

Incorrect. Security Groups control network traffic at instance level — do not define whether a sub-network is public or private. Classification is determined by the sub-network route table (road presence to Internet Gateway). Even with a door 80 open in SG, no route to IGW, the instance is not accessible from the internet.
